title: Relationships and social life
focus: somporko, biswas, biswasghatokota, somman, bojhapora, jhogra mitiye newa, manabhiman, lokjon, nimontron, adda, bhodrota, mon rakha, songsar, dekha-shona, alada hoye jawa
body:
Family talk covers who is who. This lesson covers what goes on between people: trust, respect, falling out, making up, marriage and the Kolkata social calendar of invitations and adda. Several of these words (manabhiman, adda, lokikota) have no clean English equivalent, so learn them from the examples.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| somporko | সম্পর্ক | relationship |
| biswas | বিশ্বাস | trust |
| biswasghatokota | বিশ্বাসঘাতকতা | betrayal |
| somman | সম্মান | respect |
| bojhapora | বোঝাপড়া | mutual understanding |
| manabhiman | মান-অভিমান | sulking, hurt feelings |
| adda | আড্ডা | long relaxed chat |
| bhodrota | ভদ্রতা | courtesy |
| songsar | সংসার | household life |
| dekha-shona | দেখাশোনা | arranged-marriage meeting |
| alada hoye jawa | আলাদা হয়ে যাওয়া | to separate |
| lokikota | লৌকিকতা | social obligations |

## Which word?

**obhiman vs rag.** rag is anger. obhiman is the quiet hurt you feel toward someone close who should have known better. You sulk, and you expect them to notice. manabhiman is the back-and-forth of it.

**nimontron vs nemontonno.** Same word. Say nemontonno; nimontron is for printed cards and formal writing.

**bojhapora vs bhul bojhabujhi.** bojhapora is understanding that works (or settling things). bhul bojhabujhi is a misunderstanding.

**alada hoye jawa vs bichhed vs divorce.** In conversation say divorce or alada hoye gechhe. bichhed is newspaper Bengali.

**mon rakha vs somman kora.** somman kora is real respect. mon rakha is going along with someone to keep them happy, often without meaning it.

## Examples

- or opor ar biswas nei: I don't trust him any more
- dujon-er modhye bojhapora-ta darun: The two of them have a great understanding
- shudhu mon rakhar jonno kotha-ta mene nilam: I only agreed to keep him happy
- chol, Coffee House-e adda dite jai: Come on, let's go hang out at Coffee House
- ma-r ekhono obhiman, phone korini bole: Ma's still hurt that I didn't call
- dekha-shona-r din chhele-r bari theke chhoy jon esechhilo: Six people came from the boy's side for the meeting
- bhodrota kore ek-bar dhonnobad to bolte parto: He could at least have said thank you out of courtesy
- kharap somoy-e kara pashe thake, tokhon-i bojha jay: You find out who stands by you in bad times
- lokikota-r chape pujo-r sob nemontonno rakhte hoy: Social pressure means you have to attend every Puja invitation
- koto din por dekha! ki khobor?: It's been ages! What's new?

cards.Example: or songe amar somporko-ta ekhon bhalo na: My relationship with her isn't good right now
cards.Notes: Any relationship: family, work, romantic. somporko-e achhi = I'm in a relationship. Also 'connection' between ideas.

cards.Example: ek bar biswas bhenge gele ar fire ashe na: Once trust is broken it doesn't come back
cards.Notes: Also belief/faith. biswas kora = to trust or believe; bharsa is a casual synonym for reliance (or opor bharsa nei).

cards.Example: eta-ke ami biswasghatokota chhara ar kichhu bolbo na: I'd call this nothing but betrayal
cards.Notes: biswasghatok = traitor. Strong word; for a lighter 'let me down' say dhoka dewa.

cards.Example: boro-der somman korte shekho: Learn to respect your elders
cards.Notes: Also honour/prestige (somman haranor bhoy = fear of losing face). shroddha is deeper reverence.

cards.Example: ora dujon-er modhye bojhapora khub bhalo: The two of them understand each other really well
cards.Notes: Also a settling of accounts after a dispute: ek-ta bojhapora kore nao = sort it out between you.

cards.English: to make up after a fight
cards.Example: tomra dujon jhogra-ta mitiye nao: You two should make up
cards.Notes: mitiye newa alone also settles a dispute or a bill; mitmat = reconciled.

cards.English: sulking / hurt feelings (between people who are close)
cards.Example: ma-meye-r modhye manabhiman lege-i thake: Mother and daughter are always sulking at each other
cards.Notes: obhiman is hurt pride with someone you love; rag is plain anger. A very Bengali concept.

cards.Example: bari-te aaj onek lokjon ashbe: Lots of people are coming to the house today
cards.Notes: Plural and vague: guests, a crowd, people around. lok alone is one person or 'people' in sayings.

cards.English: invitation (formal word, as on a printed card)
cards.Example: biye-r nimontron potro eshechhe: The wedding invitation card has come
cards.Notes: In speech everyone says nemontonno (nemontonno kora = invite); nimontron is written or formal.

cards.Example: rabibar sokale para-r chayer dokan-e adda chole: On Sunday mornings there's a chat session at the local tea stall
cards.Notes: adda dewa = to hang out chatting. addabaaj = someone who loves adda. Not idle gossip; it's a Kolkata institution.

cards.Example: bhodrota kore ek-bar phone to korte parto: Out of courtesy he could at least have called
cards.Notes: bhodro = polite; obhodro = rude. bhodrota kore = out of politeness.

cards.English: to humour someone / keep someone happy
cards.Example: shudhu or mon rakhar jonno haan bollam: I only said yes to keep her happy
cards.Notes: Often slightly negative: doing something you don't mean to avoid hurting someone. mon bhanga = to hurt someone.

cards.Example: biye-r por songsar samlate giye or gaan chhere gelo: After marriage, running the household made her give up singing
cards.Notes: songsar kora = to run a household / be married. songsari = family-minded.

cards.English: arranged-marriage meeting (families meet a prospective match)
cards.Example: kal meye-r dekha-shona achhe: The families are meeting about the girl's match tomorrow
cards.Notes: Also means looking after (baba-ma-r dekha-shona kora); context tells you which.

cards.Example: ora prem kore biye korechhe, sombondho kore na: They had a love marriage, not an arranged one
cards.Notes: sombondho = a marriage proposal between families. Love marriage is said in English or prem kore biye.

cards.English: to date / be in a romantic relationship
cards.Example: ora college theke prem korchhe: They've been dating since college
cards.Notes: Kolkata's standard word; going out and dating are also said by young people.

cards.Example: biye-r dosh bochhor por ora alada hoye gelo: They separated after ten years of marriage
cards.Notes: Neutral and polite; divorce is said in English, bibaho bichhed is the formal term.

cards.Example: or bichhed-er khobor shune sobai obak: Everyone was shocked to hear of their divorce
cards.Notes: Formal or literary; also 'parting' in songs. Speech prefers divorce or alada hoye jawa.

cards.Example: amader bondhutto kuri bochhorer: Our friendship goes back twenty years
cards.Notes: bondhutto kora = to make friends; bondhutto bhanga = a friendship ending.

cards.Example: tomake amar boss-er songe porichoy koriye dichhi: Let me introduce you to my boss
cards.Notes: porichoy = acquaintance or identity; porichito = acquainted.

cards.English: to check in on someone (how they're doing)
cards.Example: mashi-r shorir kharap, ek-bar khoj nio: Aunt isn't well, check in on her
cards.Notes: Not keeping in touch at all is: kono khoj rakhe na.

cards.English: to taunt / rub someone's nose in something
cards.Example: taka dhar diyechhe bole bar bar khota dey: He keeps throwing it in my face that he lent me money
cards.Notes: Typical of family fights: reminding someone of a past favour or failure.

cards.Example: kharap somoy-e o amar pashe chhilo: She stood by me in hard times
cards.Notes: pashe dandano = to step up and support. Common in condolences and speeches.

cards.Example: o kaaro songe mela-mesha kore na: He doesn't mix with anyone
cards.Notes: Can hint at disapproval of company: oder songe mela-mesha koro na.

cards.Example: lokikota-r jonno biye-te jete holo: I had to go to the wedding out of social obligation
cards.Notes: Gifts, visits and invitations you return because it's expected.

cards.English: to accept someone as one's own
cards.Example: shoshur-bari-r sobai amake apon kore niyechhe: My in-laws have welcomed me as one of their own
cards.Notes: apon = one's own, close; por = an outsider.

cards.English: Give my regards to your parents.
cards.Notes: Friends' parents are kaku-kakima in Kolkata; pronam for elders, bhalobasha for younger people.

cards.English: It's been ages since we met!
cards.Notes: The standard greeting on running into someone; often followed by ki khobor?
